traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Ulmaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; margins entire or dentate; veins pinnate or palmate; leaves evergreen or deciduous; stipules present; plants hermaphrodite, monoecious or polygamous; ovary superior; floral cup present or absent; stems woody; flowers solitary or in cymes; flowers actinomorphic or zygomorphic; perianth tepals; fruit samara, nut or drupe; stamens (2-) 4 to 8 (-15); carpels 2 (-3). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 329, family Ulmaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral becoming distichous, usually; read as {"distichous": "often", "spiral": "often"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: DELTA Ulmaceae (read 2026-10-17): flowers single or grouped, the groups being axillary cymes or fascicles and mostly cymose clusters; elm flowers come in clustered fascicles, which draw as small cymes. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Simpson (2019) p. 329: margins serrate. Watson and Dallwitz's DELTA gave entire or dentate, its word for any toothed edge; elm and zelkova teeth point forward, so serrate, with entire for the few smooth-edged members. Jay 2026-10-15 ~06:32Z: "go with your recommendations on disagreements".

traits.leaf_venation.note: DELTA Ulmaceae (read 2026-10-17) ties the three-veined palmate leaf to Celtidoideae only, a group its own remarks say now sits in Cannabaceae; the APG family left (Ulmus, Zelkova, Ampelocera, Holoptelea, Phyllostylon, Planera, Hemiptelea; 56 spp per Fu et al. 2021, MDPI Plants) is the pinnately veined elm subfamily.

traits.leaf_habit.note: DELTA Ulmaceae (read 2026-10-17) gives leaves persistent or deciduous; the MDPI Plants biogeographic overview of the 7-genus family (read 2026-10-17) calls the family deciduous and only rarely evergreen, and Wikipedia Ulmus (~35 of 56 spp) describes elms as deciduous or semi-deciduous; the evergreen side is the small tropical clade (Ampelocera and kin, ~13 spp).

traits.sexual_system.note: DELTA Ulmaceae (read 2026-10-17): hermaphrodite, monoecious or polygamomonoecious. Weighted by genus: Wikipedia Ulmus (~35 spp) has perfect apetalous flowers; the MDPI Plants overview (read 2026-10-17) gives Zelkova (6) and Planera (1) mixed male, female and perfect flowers on one plant (polygamous); the remaining ~13 tropical species not counted. Ulmus alone is about 35 of 56 species.

traits.fruit_type.note: MDPI Plants biogeographic overview of Ulmaceae (read 2026-10-17; 7 genera, 56 spp) and Wikipedia Ulmus (read 2026-10-17): winged wind-borne fruits in Ulmus (~35 spp, samara), Holoptelea and Phyllostylon (part of 13 tropical spp) and the half-winged Hemiptelea (1); unwinged drupe-like fruits in Zelkova (6, achene-like nutlet), Ampelocera (drupes) and Planera (1). Winged fruits are roughly 40 of 56 species. DELTA lists samara, nut or drupe.
